The visual and numeric evidence agree on a mixed result: lowering tail lag from `0.80` to `0.75` preserves the same self-propelled turn-and-capture route and improves arrival, distance, and effort, but it does not reduce posterior excursion or cap contact and it raises force/moment loads. I’ll record that diagnosis first, then test one isolated posterior-damping change on top of the measured `0.75` anchor.

The candidate now keeps the measured `0.75` tail-lag anchor and changes only posterior damping to `0.70` relative to that anchor. I’ve also distilled the prior rollout’s mixed positive/negative lesson into durable guidance; next I’m checking the exact edits and running the workspace’s required guard suite (no CFD).
